name: Corporate Acquisition Likelihood Model
description: This dataset provides predictive rankings of publicly traded companies most likely to be acquired within the next year. It leverages both advanced natural language processing of global news articles and analysis of structured financial and corporate data, including M&A activity, proxy fights, credit risk, and valuation metrics. By combining text-based signals with fundamental indicators, the model offers percentile scores across global, regional, sector, and industry levels, as well as flags for recent corporate actions. Investors and analysts can use these insights to identify potential takeover targets, anticipate price movements driven by acquisition speculation, and inform event-driven trading strategies.

name: AI Equity Alpha Forecasts
description: This dataset provides machine learning-driven forecasts of total return alpha for a broad universe of listed equities, with prediction horizons ranging from 1 to 12 months. It includes a comprehensive set of 291 explainability factors per stock, spanning areas such as accounting forensics, sentiment analysis, business model clarity, technical indicators, credit risk, valuation models, and more. The dataset delivers both daily and weekly updates, offering granular insights into the drivers of predicted returns. By combining forward-looking alpha scores with detailed factor breakdowns, this resource enables researchers and quantitative analysts to identify potential outperformers, understand the underlying reasons for forecasts, and enhance equity selection and risk management strategies. Its breadth and depth make it a valuable tool for predicting price movements and constructing robust investment models.

name: AI Enhanced Equity Factor Transfer
description: This dataset leverages advanced AI techniques to extract and transfer high-level equity factor features from a sophisticated quantitative research framework to other datasets. It includes a rich set of features such as price momentum, money flow strength, volume anomalies, liquidity alignment, and technical indicators like Bollinger Bands and Williams %R. Each feature is semantically defined and generated through AI-driven processes, ensuring clarity and consistency. By capturing nuanced interactions between price, volume, and liquidity, the dataset provides actionable signals for predicting price movements and constructing robust quantitative models. Its transfer learning approach enables the application of proven factor knowledge across diverse datasets, enhancing the predictive power and adaptability of investment strategies.

name: AI News Sentiment Scores
description: This dataset provides daily sentiment scores for global equities by analyzing news articles, press releases, and regulatory disclosures using a proprietary transformer-based natural language processing model. Covering thousands of companies across major regions, it quantifies the tone and relevance of news events, offering granular sentiment metrics at both the entity and event level. By systematically capturing shifts in market sentiment and event novelty, the dataset enables researchers and investors to identify potential price-moving signals, enhance alpha generation, and improve risk management. Its comprehensive coverage and advanced scoring methodology make it a valuable resource for predicting short-term and medium-term asset returns based on news-driven market dynamics.

name: Performance-Weighted Analyst Estimates
description: This dataset applies an enhanced version of the StarMine SmartEstimate model to a broad universe of stocks and financial metrics, leveraging analyst estimate data from IBES. It calculates a performance score for each analyst based on their historical forecasting accuracy and incorporates the recency of their estimates. By combining these two factors, the model generates "smart estimates" that are more predictive than simple consensus means. The dataset includes modules for analyst innovation, outlier handling, and time-series feature generation, making it a robust tool for identifying which analyst forecasts are likely to be most accurate. This can help investors and researchers anticipate earnings surprises and price movements, as changes in smart estimates often precede market reactions.

name: ESG scores
description: This dataset provides a comprehensive mapping between Reuters Instrument Codes (RICs) and Bloomberg Identifiers (BBIDs), facilitating cross-platform security identification and data integration. By linking these two widely used financial identifiers, the dataset enables seamless aggregation and comparison of market data from Bloomberg and Refinitiv sources. This mapping is essential for portfolio managers, researchers, and trading systems that require accurate and efficient reconciliation of securities across different data vendors. While not directly predictive of price movements, the dataset is crucial for ensuring data integrity and consistency in multi-source financial analysis, which underpins robust quantitative research and trading strategies.

researchPapers.title: Research Paper: ESG Preference, Institutional Trading, and Stock Return Patterns
Research Paper: Corporate ESG Profiles and Investor Horizons

name: Estimations of Key Fundamentals
description: This dataset provides daily, regionally split files containing detailed and consensus analyst estimates for key financial metrics such as revenue, EBITDA, EPS, dividends, and price targets for publicly traded companies worldwide. It includes individual analyst and broker forecasts, consensus calculations (mean, median, high, low, standard deviation), and actuals, along with metadata on fiscal periods, reporting currencies, and company identifiers. The dataset is highly granular, supporting point-in-time analysis and backtesting, and is essential for identifying earnings surprises, revisions, and trends in analyst sentiment. By tracking changes in consensus and individual estimates, users can anticipate price movements driven by earnings releases, analyst upgrades/downgrades, and shifts in market expectations.

researchPapers.title: Research Paper: Investor Learning, Earnings Signals, and Stock Returns
Research Paper: Factor Investing: Get Your Exposures Right!

name: Earnings forecasts
description: This dataset provides bottom-up aggregated earnings forecasts and related financial metrics at the country, sector, industry, and index levels, covering 56 countries and major international indices with history back to 1985. It includes consensus analyst estimates for key measures such as EPS, revenue, book value, cash flow, dividends, P/E ratios, and long-term growth, all calendarized and available in local and common currencies. The data is structured to support global asset allocation, cross-border valuation, sector and industry analysis, and derivatives research. By tracking changes in consensus, estimate revisions, and aggregated sentiment, the dataset enables investors to identify under- or overvalued markets, monitor macro and sector trends, and anticipate shifts in market sentiment—making it a valuable tool for predicting price movements at both the index and sector level.

name: Real Time Estimates
description: This dataset provides a comprehensive mapping between Bloomberg IDs (BBIDs) and Reuters Instrument Codes (RICs), facilitating cross-referencing of securities across two major financial data platforms. The mapping is maintained and updated to ensure accurate linkage, supporting workflows that require integration of Bloomberg and Reuters data, such as security master management, trade reconciliation, and multi-vendor analytics. While not intended for general research or direct price prediction, the dataset is essential for ensuring data consistency and completeness in quantitative models and operational processes that rely on both Bloomberg and Reuters identifiers.

researchPapers.title: Creating D0 Alphas with Analyst Data

name: ESG Model
description: This dataset provides comprehensive Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) factor scores for publicly traded companies worldwide. It includes detailed metrics across the E, S, and G pillars, such as board diversity, environmental efficiency, workforce equality, and shareholder rights, along with integrated ratings that combine financial and extra-financial health. The data is structured for quantitative analysis, enabling users to assess a company’s sustainability profile and long-term risk. By incorporating these ESG factors into investment models, analysts can identify companies with superior sustainability practices, which have been shown to correlate with improved risk-adjusted returns and can be used to predict future price movements and portfolio performance.

name: Analyst Estimate Data for Equity
description: This dataset provides intraday updates of consensus financial estimates, actuals, and company guidance for over 16,000 global companies, sourced from more than 800 contributing brokers. It includes multiple daily delta files per region, allowing users to track real-time changes in analyst expectations for key financial metrics such as EPS, sales, dividends, cash flow, and industry-specific items. The dataset also offers daily historical consensus timelines, enabling analysis of estimate revisions, surprises, and trends. By capturing the latest market sentiment and analyst forecasts, this data is highly valuable for predicting price movements, identifying earnings momentum, and responding to market-moving events as they unfold.

researchPapers.title: Creating D0 Alphas with Analyst Data

name: Integrated Broker Estimates
description: WQ SmartData is an intermediate data platform that provides value-added, idea-embedded data managers and analytics for financial and event datasets. It includes advanced processing such as event classification (e.g., M&A, earnings), group clustering, natural language processing of textual data (e.g., EDGAR filings, news sentiment), and graph/network analytics. By integrating and transforming raw data from sources like FactSet, RavenPack, and EDGAR, it enables researchers to extract features, signals, and event-driven alphas that are difficult to obtain from raw feeds, supporting innovative quantitative strategies and improving the predictive power of models for price movements.

researchPapers.title: Research Paper: Non-GAAP Earnings and the Earnings Quality Trade-off

name: Analyst Trade Ideas
description: This dataset provides a comprehensive mapping between Bloomberg IDs (BBIDs) and Refinitiv Instrument Codes (RICs), facilitating cross-platform identification of securities. It is sourced from both Bloomberg and Refinitiv, ensuring high coverage and accuracy. While not intended for general research or direct price prediction, this mapping is essential for data integration, enabling analysts and portfolio managers to link and synchronize datasets from different vendors. By ensuring consistent instrument identification, it supports robust multi-source analytics, backtesting, and the construction of unified trading universes, which are foundational for any quantitative or fundamental price movement analysis.

name: Dividend estimation data
description: This dataset provides a comprehensive mapping between Reuters Instrument Codes (RIC) and Bloomberg identifiers for financial securities. It is essential for cross-referencing and integrating data from different financial data providers, enabling analysts and systems to unify disparate datasets for more robust analysis. While it does not directly contain price or fundamental data, its utility lies in facilitating accurate data merging, which is crucial for building reliable models and conducting multi-source research that can ultimately improve price movement predictions.

name: Analyst Estimation Data
description: This dataset provides comprehensive fundamental data and analyst-driven rankings for over 1,700 primarily US-listed securities, with some international coverage. It includes detailed historical and estimated metrics such as earnings, sales, dividends, valuation ratios, and proprietary rankings for timeliness, safety, and technical performance. The dataset also features forward-looking projections, growth rates, and risk measures, updated monthly until 2014 and weekly thereafter. By combining quantitative financials with qualitative analyst assessments, this resource is valuable for predicting price movements, identifying outperformers, and constructing factor-based or risk-managed investment strategies.

name: Financial Statement Data
description: The SNL Insurance dataset provides comprehensive financial, operational, and structural data on U.S. and global insurance companies, including property & casualty, life, health, and reinsurance sectors. It covers detailed company profiles, ownership structures, security-level information (common and preferred equity, senior and subordinated debt), and a wide array of financial statement items such as assets, liabilities, equity, premiums, claims, reserves, investment portfolios, and profitability metrics. The dataset also includes regulatory filings, capital offerings, and segment-level data, enabling peer comparisons and in-depth analysis of insurance company performance, risk, and capital adequacy. This rich, timely data is essential for building predictive models of price movements, as it allows for the identification of trends in earnings, capital strength, underwriting results, and market positioning—key drivers of insurance stock valuations and risk premia.

name: Fundamental Analyst Estimates
description: The FactSet Fundamental dataset provides comprehensive annual and interim financial statement data, ratios, and per-share metrics for global companies, with coverage starting from 1980 for developed markets and the 1990s for developing markets. The dataset includes restatements, detailed line items, and standardized fields, enabling robust cross-company and cross-market comparisons. Key fields include balance sheet, income statement, and cash flow items, as well as derived ratios such as return on equity, margins, and growth rates. This dataset is valuable for quantitative and fundamental analysis, backtesting, and predictive modeling, as it allows users to track historical financial performance, identify trends, and build factor models that can help forecast future price movements based on company fundamentals.

name: Broker Estimates
description: This dataset provides concise, real-time summaries of major company news events that are likely to move markets. Each event is tagged by topic (such as M&A, earnings guidance, product launches, regulatory actions, and more) and assigned a significance level, allowing users to filter for the most impactful developments. The data includes detailed headlines, descriptions, event categorization, and metadata such as company identifiers, event timing, and industry classification. By focusing on material news and filtering out less relevant information, this dataset enables quantitative analysts and traders to integrate event-driven signals into their models, backtest the impact of specific news types, and react quickly to market-moving corporate actions, thereby improving the prediction of short-term price movements and volatility.

researchPapers.title: Research Paper: Investor Learning, Earnings Signals, and Stock Returns

name: Daily Split Data
description: This dataset provides daily records of stock split and capitalization change events for global equities, including effective split dates, split factors, and related adjustment information. The data enables users to accurately adjust historical per-share financial measures (such as earnings per share, book value per share, and dividends per share) to reflect changes in share count due to splits. By ensuring that historical data is consistently adjusted for corporate actions, this dataset is essential for maintaining the integrity of time series analysis, backtesting, and quantitative models. Accurate split adjustment is critical for predicting price movements, as it prevents artificial jumps or drops in per-share metrics and allows for meaningful comparison of financial performance over time.

name: Analyst estimate prediction data
description: This dataset provides point-in-time, globally standardized fundamental financial data for over 47,000 active and 15,000 inactive companies across more than 100 countries. It includes daily snapshots of income statements, balance sheets, and cash flow statements, as well as original and restated values, ensuring accurate historical backtesting without forward-looking or survivorship bias. The data is available on both annual and interim bases, with coverage extending back to 1989 for US companies and 1997 for non-US companies. By offering consistent, unbiased, and comprehensive financials, this dataset enables robust factor research, model development, and performance attribution, making it highly valuable for predicting price movements based on fundamental signals and for constructing and validating systematic investment strategies.

researchPapers.title: Creating D0 Alphas with Model Data

name: Smart Conference call transcript data
description: This dataset provides comprehensive coverage of corporate and macroeconomic events, including earnings releases, conference calls, IPOs, SEC filings, and economic indicators. It includes detailed event metadata, verbatim transcripts, analyst briefs, and supporting materials such as presentations and audio recordings. The data is structured with identifiers like RIC, CUSIP, SEDOL, and ISIN, and is updated frequently with both current and historical records. By tracking the timing, content, and sentiment of key corporate events and macroeconomic announcements, this dataset enables investors and analysts to anticipate market-moving news, assess management tone and guidance, and identify catalysts that may impact stock prices and market volatility.

name: Fundamental Income and Dividend Model
description: This dataset provides a comprehensive mapping between Reuters Instrument Codes (RICs) and Bloomberg IDs (BBIDs) for financial securities. Sourced from both Bloomberg and Refinitiv, it enables users to cross-reference and integrate data from these two major financial data providers. The mapping is essential for data normalization, security master management, and ensuring consistency across different data feeds and analytics platforms. While not directly predictive of price movements, this dataset is a critical infrastructure component for quantitative research, portfolio management, and any workflow that requires accurate security identification and linkage across systems.

name: Analyst Estimates Base Reference
description: This dataset serves as a placeholder or reference point for the foundational data underlying analyst estimates and key performance indicators, without containing any actual financial or market data itself. Its primary function is to facilitate access to industry classifications and essential metadata required for quantitative research, while avoiding penalization for using common base modules in research workflows. Although it does not provide direct content, it enables seamless integration of industry and company classification information, which is crucial for constructing and interpreting analyst-driven signals and for ensuring consistency in backtesting and model development. By supporting the structural backbone for more detailed analyst and KPI datasets, it indirectly aids in the accurate prediction of price movements through proper sector and industry alignment.

name: Deep Learning Analyst Chart Signals
description: This dataset leverages deep learning to predict stock returns by mimicking how retail traders interpret analyst-driven financial charts. It transforms time series data related to analyst activity and financial measures into images, which are then processed by pre-trained convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to forecast future price movements. By capturing visual patterns and signals that may be overlooked by traditional quantitative models, this approach aims to extract alpha from the collective sentiment and revisions embedded in analyst data. The dataset is particularly useful for identifying non-linear relationships and subtle cues in analyst-driven market behavior, offering a novel edge for systematic trading strategies.

name: Standardized Analyst Consensus Forecasts
description: This dataset provides standardized, cleaned, and event-aligned analyst consensus forecasts and actuals for global equities, enabling direct comparison across companies and time. It aggregates and harmonizes consensus data from multiple leading sources, including I/B/E/S, Capital IQ, and FactSet, and applies rigorous data cleaning to remove expired or irrelevant forecasts. The dataset supports flexible configuration for different forecast horizons (quarterly, annual, rolling) and includes both forecast and actual values, as well as surprise calculations. By offering time-series event data with consistent methodology, it allows users to track revisions, analyze forecast accuracy, and construct robust quantitative models. This makes it a valuable resource for predicting price movements, backtesting strategies, and understanding market expectations versus realized outcomes.

name: Global Analyst Earnings Forecasts
description: This dataset provides comprehensive global analyst earnings forecasts, consensus estimates, and actuals for over 60,000 companies, sourced from broker and sell-side analyst submissions. It includes detailed and summary-level data on key financial metrics such as earnings per share (EPS), revenue, cash flow, and segment-level results, as well as analyst recommendations and price targets. The dataset tracks both current and historical estimates, revisions, and company-issued guidance, with extensive metadata on contributors, accounting standards, and industry classifications. By aggregating and updating analyst expectations in near real-time, this dataset enables users to monitor market sentiment, identify earnings momentum, and anticipate potential surprises—making it a valuable tool for predicting price movements and constructing quantitative investment strategies.

name: Global Analyst Factor Signals
description: This dataset provides a comprehensive suite of analyst-derived quantitative factors and indicators for global equities, constructed using standardized methodologies. It leverages consensus estimates, actuals, and revision data from multiple sources to generate a wide range of predictive signals, such as estimate momentum, earnings surprise, and analyst recommendation trends. The dataset is designed to be comparable across regions and time, with rigorous data cleaning and normalization. By offering both raw and composite factors—similar to those used in established quantitative models—this resource enables users to systematically test and implement alpha strategies, enhance risk models, and improve the forecasting of price movements based on analyst behavior and expectations.

name: Multi Horizon Analyst Revision Signals
description: This dataset provides decomposed analyst revision signals across short, medium, and long time horizons, derived from a comprehensive analyst revision-based stock ranking model. By applying advanced signal processing techniques, it extracts horizon-specific components from a wide array of analyst-driven metrics, such as earnings estimate changes, recommendation shifts, and predicted surprises. The resulting fields enable researchers and investors to isolate and analyze the impact of analyst sentiment and estimate revisions over different time frames, enhancing the ability to identify timely alpha opportunities and anticipate price movements driven by changes in analyst outlook. This multi-horizon approach is particularly valuable for constructing and testing trading strategies that are sensitive to the timing and persistence of analyst-driven signals.

name: Behavioral Finance Signal Factors
description: This dataset provides a suite of behavioral finance-based signals designed to capture investor extrapolation bias in equity markets. It includes six key factors: three that analyze the shape and curvature of price paths, and three that identify salient patterns such as streaks in returns, extreme daily movements, and visually prominent trends. By quantifying how investors may irrationally project recent performance into the future, these signals serve as contrarian indicators and can help forecast short-term reversals and momentum effects. The dataset is valuable for predictive modeling, risk assessment, and portfolio construction, offering insights into market inefficiencies driven by psychological biases and aiding in the identification of potential mispricings and alpha opportunities.

name: Bias Adjusted Analyst Forecasts
description: This dataset provides refined analyst estimates for stock price targets and fundamental metrics, with systematic analyst biases removed. By leveraging both detailed and consensus-level forecasts, it offers bias-controlled measures for key indicators such as price targets and earnings per share. The dataset includes various statistical summaries (mean, median, standard deviation, high/low values) and tracks the frequency of estimate revisions. By eliminating common sources of analyst optimism or pessimism, these bias-free estimates offer a more accurate and reliable view of market expectations. This can enhance quantitative models and investment strategies by improving the predictive power of analyst forecasts for future price movements, reducing noise, and helping to identify genuine signals of market sentiment and company performance.

name: US Board Governance and Leadership Metrics
description: This dataset provides daily, firm-level statistics on the structure, composition, and dynamics of company boards and senior management teams for publicly listed US companies. It aggregates detailed person- and board-level data into metrics such as board size, independence, gender diversity, director and executive tenure, turnover rates, and network connectivity (interlocks with other firms). Additional fields capture leadership stability (e.g., CEO and chairman tenure, duality), educational attainment, and family dominance. By quantifying governance quality, diversity, and network effects, these features offer valuable signals for predicting stock price movements, as changes in board structure, turnover, and connectivity can reflect shifts in oversight, strategic direction, and access to information, all of which are linked to future firm performance and risk.

name: Board Member Network Analysis
description: This dataset provides a comprehensive analysis of company board member networks, focusing on the connections and influence of directors across multiple firms. It includes metrics such as board strength, number of connected companies and individuals, and various network centrality scores (e.g., authority, hub, page rank, betweenness, eigen centrality). By quantifying the structure and reach of board member relationships, the dataset helps identify companies with strong strategic guidance, access to resources, and potential for superior financial performance. Investors and analysts can leverage these insights to predict price movements by assessing how board connectivity and influence may impact company growth, risk management, and competitive positioning.

name: Deep Learning Chart-Based Alpha
description: This dataset leverages deep learning to predict future stock returns by mimicking the decision-making process of retail traders who analyze price charts. It transforms time series financial data into images (such as OHLC or other chart types) and applies pre-trained convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to these images to generate return forecasts. The output includes both raw return predictions and quantile-based relative return rankings, along with associated probabilities. By capturing complex visual patterns and technical signals that may be overlooked by traditional quantitative models, this approach can identify non-linear relationships and subtle chart features that are predictive of price movements. The dataset is particularly useful for developing and testing alpha models that seek to exploit behavioral and technical trading signals, offering a novel perspective that complements standard factor-based or fundamental models.

name: Deep Learning Chart Returns Predictor
description: This dataset leverages deep learning techniques to analyze visual representations of time series financial data, such as stock price charts, to forecast future multi-horizon returns. By emulating the decision-making process of retail traders who rely on chart patterns, the dataset transforms historical price and volume data into images, which are then processed by pre-trained convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to generate predictive signals. The output includes raw and relative return predictions, quantile rankings, and probability scores for individual stocks. This approach can help identify short-term price movements and potential trading opportunities by capturing complex, non-linear patterns in market behavior that traditional quantitative models may overlook, making it a valuable tool for alpha generation and risk management in equity portfolios.

researchPapers.title: Getting started with Price Volume Datasets

name: Deep Learning Chart Return Prediction
description: This dataset leverages deep learning techniques to analyze visual representations of financial time series data, such as OHLC charts, to predict future stock returns. By imitating the decision-making process of retail traders who rely on chart patterns, the dataset transforms interval-based price and volume data into images, which are then processed by pre-trained convolutional neural networks (CNNs). The model outputs multi-horizon return predictions, quantile rankings, and probabilities for future price movements. This approach enables the identification of complex, non-linear patterns in market data that may be missed by traditional statistical methods, making it a valuable tool for forecasting short-term and medium-term price changes and enhancing trading strategies.

researchPapers.title: Getting started with Price Volume Datasets

name: Price Chart Continuation Pattern Similarity
description: This dataset provides daily, per-stock similarity scores that measure how closely a stock’s price chart matches well-known continuation-style technical patterns, such as flags, pennants, rectangles, channels, scallops, staircases, cup-and-handle, and gap formations. The scores are derived by comparing chart-image embeddings to a curated library of canonical continuation patterns using advanced machine learning techniques. Multiple summary statistics (mean, median, max, dynamic, etc.) are available across different time horizons and regions, enabling flexible analysis. These similarity scores can be used to identify stocks likely to resume their current trend after consolidation, support trend-following strategies, and enhance alpha generation by confirming or filtering trading signals. The dataset is particularly valuable for quantitative researchers seeking to incorporate pattern-based insights into predictive models for price movement forecasting.

researchPapers.title: Getting started with Price Volume Datasets

name: Commercial Real Estate Exposure Model
description: This dataset provides a quantitative measure of individual stocks’ sensitivity to the commercial real estate market, using a robust regression approach that controls for residential real estate and interest rate effects. By calculating a “commercial real estate beta” for each stock, the dataset enables investors to identify companies with high or low exposure to commercial real estate risks. Sector-level summaries and firm-specific scores help users assess portfolio vulnerability to market shifts, especially during periods of stress in real estate or credit markets. This information is valuable for risk management, portfolio construction, and tactical asset allocation, as it allows investors to hedge or adjust positions based on anticipated movements in the commercial real estate sector, potentially improving prediction of price movements for affected stocks.

name: Finance Creator Prediction Performance
description: This dataset aggregates and analyzes stock price predictions made by prominent finance content creators across platforms such as Twitter, YouTube, and select Discord channels. Using AI-driven natural language processing and computer vision, it extracts directional signals (long/short), confidence scores, and performance metrics for each creator and asset. The data includes detailed accuracy statistics, momentum indicators, and portfolio returns segmented by market conditions and time horizons. By tracking the historical success and behavioral biases of these creators, the dataset provides a unique perspective on crowd-sourced trading sentiment and can be leveraged to identify emerging trends, high-confidence signals, and potential price movements in equities.

researchPapers.title: Getting started with Social Media Datasets

name: Deep Learning Risk Free Returns
description: This dataset leverages deep learning techniques to predict risk-free returns by transforming time series price and volume data into 2D chart images, which are then analyzed using pre-trained convolutional neural networks (CNNs). The dataset includes predictions for multiple time horizons (such as 5, 10, 20, and 50 days) and provides both raw and relative return forecasts, along with quantile rankings and associated probabilities. By simulating a retail trader’s perspective through chart-based analysis, this dataset offers a unique, high-dimensional approach to forecasting future returns with minimal risk. It is particularly useful for identifying low-risk trading opportunities and enhancing portfolio construction by providing robust, model-driven signals that can help anticipate price movements in a risk-averse manner.

name: Deep Learning Volume Prediction
description: This dataset leverages deep learning techniques to predict future trading volume for stocks by analyzing time series chart images, mimicking the decision-making process of retail traders. It utilizes pre-trained convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to extract features from visual representations of financial data, such as OHLC charts and barcharts, and combines multiple uncorrelated prediction modules (including news count, price-volume averages, and direct volume data) to generate robust volume forecasts. The dataset covers all stocks and incorporates fallback logic using 20-day average volumes to ensure reliability. By providing forward-looking volume estimates, this resource can help identify periods of heightened market activity, anticipate liquidity changes, and improve the timing and risk management of price movement predictions.

researchPapers.title: Getting started with Price Volume Datasets

name: Earnings Update Emails Data
description: This dataset compiles analyst communications following company earnings releases, focusing on the sentiment and key financial metrics discussed in these emails. By classifying messages based on keywords such as guidance, EBIT, EBITDA, and EPS, and providing an overall sentiment score for each email, the dataset offers a unique perspective on market reactions and analyst outlooks. The information can be leveraged to gauge immediate market sentiment, anticipate price movements, and identify shifts in analyst expectations, making it a valuable resource for predicting short-term stock performance after earnings announcements.

name: International Findings Data
description: This dataset offers daily snapshots of international corporate events, including earnings announcements, conference calls, dividend declarations, shareholder meetings, and other key financial events. It provides detailed metadata such as event status, timing, fiscal period, and confirmation level, along with links to press releases and filings. By tracking the timing and revisions of earnings dates, dividend actions, and other corporate events, the dataset enables researchers and traders to anticipate market-moving disclosures, identify signals of management intent, and exploit calendar-based trading strategies. Its forward-looking coverage and granular event data are valuable for predicting price movements, volatility spikes, and abnormal returns around scheduled corporate actions.

name: Horizon Earnings and Calendar North America
description: This dataset provides concise, real-time summaries of major company news events that are likely to impact market prices. Each event is tagged by topic, significance level, and includes a headline and detailed description, covering a wide range of corporate actions such as mergers, acquisitions, product launches, regulatory changes, earnings guidance, and more. The data is structured for easy integration into quantitative models, allowing users to filter by region, industry, and event type. By focusing on high-impact developments and filtering out less relevant news, this dataset enables analysts and traders to quickly identify actionable events, perform historical trend analysis, and enhance event-driven trading strategies to better predict price movements.

name: Deep Learning Earnings Chart Predictions
description: This dataset leverages deep learning techniques to analyze financial time series charts, specifically focusing on earnings calendar events. By converting historical price and earnings data into images, it utilizes pre-trained convolutional neural networks to predict future stock returns over multiple horizons. The dataset includes quantile-based rankings, probability assignments, and risk-adjusted metrics, making it valuable for identifying stocks likely to outperform or underperform following earnings announcements. Its predictive signals can help traders and analysts anticipate price movements around earnings releases, enhance alpha generation, and improve portfolio decision-making by incorporating retail trader perspectives and advanced image-based modeling.

name: Earnings Event Risk Model
description: This dataset provides a comprehensive quantitative framework for assessing and forecasting the risk associated with upcoming corporate earnings announcements. It integrates options-implied volatility, historical price movements, and advanced statistical techniques to estimate the uncertainty and potential price impact of earnings events. The model identifies stocks with elevated earnings risk, flags potential short-selling candidates, and offers metrics for integrating earnings uncertainty into portfolio risk management. By quantifying earnings-induced volatility and comparing it to realized volatility, the dataset enables investors to anticipate outsized moves, optimize portfolio construction, and hedge against adverse earnings surprises, thereby improving risk-adjusted performance during earnings season.

name: Global Earnings Call Sentiment Matrix
description: This dataset provides a structured, matrix-format aggregation of global company earnings call transcripts, focusing on sentiment and topic analytics. It leverages advanced natural language processing to extract and quantify positive, neutral, and negative sentiment probabilities from management presentations and Q&A sessions, across over 200 thematic topics. The data is filtered and enhanced with smart aggregation techniques, including rolling and daily sentiment measures, confidence scores, and relevance indicators. By capturing nuanced shifts in management tone and analyst reactions, the dataset enables researchers and investors to identify patterns and signals that may precede price movements, offering valuable insights for predictive modeling and alpha generation in equity markets.

name: Earnings Call Text Embedding Analytics
description: This dataset provides advanced quantitative features derived from the full text of US corporate earnings call transcripts. By transforming entire transcripts into high-dimensional text embeddings and applying machine learning techniques, it captures nuanced management-analyst interactions, sentiment, and narrative shifts. The dataset includes both raw and compressed embedding vectors, event-aligned metrics, and machine-generated signals such as narrative shock magnitude and projected present value. These features enable systematic analysis of qualitative information, offering predictive insights into short-term stock price movements by quantifying tone, sentiment surprises, and narrative changes that may not be immediately reflected in market prices.

name: Multi Aspect Earnings Call Sentiment
description: This dataset provides advanced, multi-aspect sentiment analysis of earnings call transcripts for thousands of public companies across the US and Europe. Using state-of-the-art natural language processing and knowledge distillation from large language models, it evaluates sentiment across key financial dimensions such as asset utilization, profitability, leverage, valuation, and cash flow. The transcripts are segmented into presentation, question, and answer sections, with chunk-wise and summary sentiment scores available for each. Binary indicators and relevance scores help filter for the most impactful segments. By quantifying positive, negative, and neutral sentiment at granular and summary levels, the dataset enables investors and researchers to detect shifts in management tone, analyst sentiment, and market outlook, providing valuable signals for predicting future price movements and earnings surprises.

name: International Equity Forum Activity
description: This dataset compiles user engagement and sentiment metrics from a wide range of online forums dedicated to equity discussions across multiple countries and languages. It includes aggregated statistics such as active user counts, comment volumes, buy and sell ratings, and unique user participation for various financial instruments. By analyzing trends in forum activity and sentiment, the dataset provides valuable insights into retail investor behavior and crowd sentiment, which can serve as leading indicators for price movements. The inclusion of risk-adjusted performance metrics and benchmark correlations further enhances its utility for developing predictive models and alpha strategies based on social media-driven market signals.

name: US Equity KPI Forecasts
description: This dataset provides forward-looking forecasts of key financial performance indicators for approximately 1,500 US-listed companies, tailored to each firm's sector and business model. Metrics commonly include revenue, gross earnings, EBITDA, and product or segment-level financials, with additional industry-specific KPIs where relevant. The forecasts are generated using an ensemble model that integrates data from over a thousand sources, including public filings and industry data. Each forecast is accompanied by measures of historical accuracy, consensus comparison, and model confidence, enabling users to assess the reliability and potential edge of the predictions. By offering granular, company-level forecasts ahead of earnings releases, this dataset is valuable for anticipating earnings surprises, sector trends, and price movements, supporting strategies such as event-driven trading, portfolio rotation, and risk management.

name: Text-Based Event Relationship Analysis
description: This dataset leverages advanced language models to extract and classify relationships between companies, events, and entities from unstructured text sources such as news articles, press releases, and corporate communications. By identifying the types and directions of these relationships, the dataset provides structured insights into how companies interact, form alliances, or respond to market developments. This information is valuable for predicting price movements, as changes in company relationships—such as mergers, partnerships, or competitive actions—often precede significant market reactions. The dataset enhances traditional event-driven strategies by offering a deeper, more nuanced understanding of the connections and influences within the market ecosystem.

name: Deep Learning Event Return Prediction
description: This dataset leverages deep learning techniques to predict future stock returns based on event-driven financial data. By transforming time series data—such as price, volume, and event occurrences—into chart images that mimic the perspective of retail traders, the dataset enables convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to extract predictive features. It incorporates modules for handling earnings, news counts, and macroeconomic indicators, and provides both raw and relative return forecasts across multiple time horizons. The dataset is designed to capture the impact of corporate events, news flow, and market sentiment on asset prices, offering actionable signals for long and short trading strategies. Its multi-horizon, cross-sectional ranking and probability outputs make it a powerful tool for anticipating price movements and generating alpha in quantitative trading models.

name: Corporate Event Sentiment Signals
description: This dataset provides structured sentiment analysis and key driver metrics derived from corporate event transcripts, including earnings calls, company presentations, analyst/investor days, and guidance calls. It covers a global universe of public companies, with detailed metadata such as industry classification, identifiers, event timestamps, and document sections. The dataset quantifies sentiment at multiple granularities—overall, by section, and by key topic—using scores based on positive and negative event counts, polarity, and word counts. By capturing management and analyst tone, margin and pricing power sentiment, and deception signals, it enables investors and researchers to assess market expectations, information asymmetry, and the impact of qualitative disclosures on price movements. These insights can be used to forecast earnings surprises, volatility, and post-event price drift, supporting both discretionary and quantitative investment strategies.

name: Corporate Event Driven Stock Model
description: This dataset provides a systematic stock-selection model that leverages corporate event data and machine learning techniques to predict future stock returns. It incorporates a wide range of event types, such as earnings announcements, executive changes, product launches, and structural corporate actions, and processes them using advanced feature engineering and algorithms like elastic net and xgBoost. The model outputs normalized scores and ranks for stocks based on the predictive impact of these events, enabling users to identify potential alpha opportunities and construct long/short portfolios. By capturing both fundamental and behavioral signals from event-driven market reactions, the dataset is valuable for forecasting price movements, managing risk, and enhancing quantitative investment strategies.

name: Equity Expected Move Metrics
description: This dataset provides quantitative estimates of the expected price movement for equities over specified time horizons, derived from options market data and volatility metrics. It includes several approaches to calculating expected moves, such as Gaussian and log-normal models, as well as straddle and strangle-based strategies. The dataset also incorporates daily option volume and liquidity filters to ensure robustness. By capturing the market's consensus on future volatility and directional risk, these metrics can be valuable for forecasting price swings, managing risk, and identifying trading opportunities ahead of major market events or earnings releases.

name: Regulatory Filing Sentiment Analytics
description: This dataset provides detailed sentiment analysis of regulatory filings, including annual, quarterly, and event-driven reports submitted by public companies. It parses filings into standardized sections and applies advanced natural language processing to quantify positive and negative sentiment, track changes over time, and summarize key sections such as risk factors and management discussion. By measuring shifts in sentiment, word counts, and thematic topics, the dataset enables investors and analysts to detect changes in corporate tone, risk disclosure, and outlook, which can be predictive of future price movements. The ability to compare historical baselines and monitor sentiment trends across filings offers valuable insights for forecasting returns, identifying market inefficiencies, and constructing alpha-generating strategies.

name: Transformer Based Financial News Scores
description: This dataset provides daily sentiment and relevance scores for financial news articles using a custom transformer-based natural language processing model. It processes real-time news feeds, extracting and quantifying sentiment, significance, and company-level impact in a structured matrix format. By bridging the gap between raw news data and actionable signals, the dataset enables researchers and portfolio managers to efficiently identify market-moving news and assess its potential effect on asset prices. The sentiment and relevance scores can be used to enhance predictive models for price movements, support event-driven trading strategies, and diversify signal sources across companies and sectors.

name: Global Stock Forum Sentiment Signals
description: This dataset aggregates and enriches natural language data from major stock discussion forums across Korea, France, and Germany, focusing on retail investor conversations. By applying advanced NLP techniques, it extracts sentiment, opinion strength, and discussion volume at the stock level, providing a comprehensive view of investor mood and activity in these markets. The dataset enables quantitative analysis of crowd sentiment, which can be a leading indicator of price movements, especially in markets where retail participation is significant. By tracking shifts in sentiment and discussion intensity, users can identify potential inflection points, momentum changes, and emerging trends, making it a valuable tool for predicting short-term price action and enhancing trading strategies.

name: Forward Beta Risk Prediction Model
description: This dataset provides forward-looking estimates of stock beta for U.S. companies, predicting their sensitivity to market movements over the next three months. The model leverages a combination of fundamental, technical, and historical data to generate more accurate beta forecasts than traditional backward-looking measures. It includes alternative risk metrics, uncertainty bands, and risk surprise probabilities, enabling investors to assess systematic risk and anticipate potential volatility shifts. By identifying stocks with changing risk profiles, the dataset supports portfolio construction, risk management, and alpha generation strategies, making it a valuable tool for predicting price movements and managing exposure to market risk.

name: Global Institutional Fund Holdings
description: This dataset provides daily, account-level insights into the holdings and transactions of major institutional investors, including mutual funds, ETFs, asset managers, pension funds, and insurance companies. It features detailed tables on daily trades, holdings, and the size of the investment account panel, with metrics such as conviction holdings, boundary trades, significant transactions, and concentration measures. By tracking changes in institutional ownership, trade activity, and portfolio concentration, the dataset enables users to identify shifts in market sentiment, detect accumulation or liquidation trends, and assess the impact of large fund movements on individual securities. These insights are valuable for predicting price movements, understanding liquidity dynamics, and generating alpha through analysis of institutional behavior.

name: Management and Executive Data
description: This dataset provides comprehensive biographical and professional information on board members and senior executives from companies worldwide. It includes details such as employment history, education, achievements, compensation, board roles, committee memberships, and network connections across organizations. By analyzing board composition, director expertise, compensation structures, and interlocking directorates, investors and researchers can assess governance quality, leadership stability, and potential strategic shifts. These insights are valuable for predicting price movements, as changes in executive leadership, board structure, or director networks often precede significant corporate actions, impact investor sentiment, and influence firm performance.

name: Press Release Data
description: This dataset contains press release information from public companies, typically published a few days before formal SEC filings such as 10-K and 10-Q reports. It includes preliminary earnings announcements, non-GAAP financial metrics, company guidance, and key operating metrics. By providing early insights into company performance and management expectations, the dataset enables investors and analysts to anticipate price movements ahead of official filings. The data is useful for identifying trends, outliers, and market sentiment, making it valuable for short-term trading strategies and event-driven analysis.

description: This dataset provides comprehensive tracking of director and officer changes for US public companies, including appointments, resignations, dismissals, and other board or executive movements as disclosed in SEC filings (primarily Form 8-K Item 5.02). By monitoring these governance events, investors and analysts can identify potential signals of corporate strategy shifts, management instability, or governance improvements, all of which may precede significant price movements. The dataset is particularly valuable for event-driven strategies, risk assessment, and understanding the impact of leadership changes on company performance.

name: Direct Fundamental Data
description: The FactSet Fundamental dataset provides comprehensive annual and interim financial statement data, ratios, and per-share metrics for global equities, with coverage starting from 1980 for developed markets and the 1990s for emerging markets. The dataset includes restated data from 2004 onward, ensuring historical accuracy and comparability. Key fields cover balance sheet, income statement, and cash flow items, as well as detailed breakdowns of assets, liabilities, equity, revenues, expenses, and key performance indicators. FactSet’s symbology enables robust cross-referencing with other datasets. This dataset is valuable for quantitative and fundamental analysis, backtesting, and model development, as it allows researchers to track company financial health, valuation, and performance over time, supporting predictive modeling of price movements based on changes in core financial metrics.

By enabling users to drill down into historical and cross-company footnote information, the dataset offers unique insights into accounting policies, risk exposures, and non-standard financial events. Such depth of information can help analysts identify hidden risks, spot trends in corporate behavior, and improve the accuracy of fundamental models for predicting price movements.

name: ESG Scores Data
description: This dataset provides comprehensive, real-time Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) scores and analytics for over 8,000 publicly traded companies worldwide. Leveraging artificial intelligence and natural language processing, it continuously aggregates and analyzes unstructured data from news, reports, and other sources to generate daily, short-term (Pulse), long-term (Insight), and momentum-based ESG scores across 30 SASB-defined categories. The dataset includes granular category-level scores, industry percentiles, and volume metrics, enabling users to track both overall and material ESG issues relevant to each industry. By capturing both the sentiment and frequency of ESG-related events, this data helps investors identify emerging risks, controversies, and positive trends that may impact stock prices, support alpha generation, and enhance risk management in investment strategies.

name: Fundamental Point in Time Data
description: This dataset provides point-in-time, globally standardized fundamental financial data for over 60,000 companies, including both active and inactive firms, with daily granularity. It includes original and restated values for income statements, balance sheets, and cash flow statements, as well as business and geographic segment data, ratios, and company metadata. The point-in-time structure eliminates forward-looking and survivorship biases, enabling accurate historical backtesting and model development. With coverage dating back to 1989 for US companies and 1997 for non-US, this dataset is essential for constructing robust factor models, event studies, and alpha signals based on true historical financials, supporting reliable prediction of price movements and risk assessment.

description: This dataset provides comprehensive fundamental data on over 20,000 U.S. financial institutions, including publicly traded and privately held banks, thrifts, and credit unions. It features timely updates from regulatory filings and earnings releases, covering key financial metrics such as product pricing, loan mix, credit quality, net interest margin, efficiency ratio, and more. The dataset enables peer comparisons, market share analysis, and geographic footprint evaluation, making it valuable for both operators and investors. By analyzing trends in profitability, asset quality, capital adequacy, and operational efficiency, users can identify financial strengths and weaknesses, anticipate strategic moves, and predict price movements in the banking sector.

description: This dataset provides comprehensive, point-in-time global fundamental financial data for public companies, capturing daily snapshots of balance sheet, income statement, and cash flow items as originally reported and as subsequently restated. The point-in-time methodology ensures that each data value reflects what was known to the market at specific historical dates, minimizing look-ahead bias and enabling accurate backtesting and historical analysis. This dataset is invaluable for quantitative research, factor modeling, and alpha generation, as it allows users to analyze the evolution of company fundamentals, detect restatements, and assess the impact of financial statement changes on stock price movements.

name: Earnings Tax Data
description: This dataset provides comprehensive, point-in-time fundamental financial data for public companies worldwide, with annual history dating back to 1980 for developed markets and the 1990s for developing markets. It includes detailed financial statement items, ratios, per-share data, and key performance indicators, all mapped to unique company and security identifiers. The data covers balance sheets, income statements, cash flows, segment information, and restatements, enabling robust analysis of company performance, valuation, and risk. By offering granular, timely, and historically consistent financial metrics, this dataset is essential for building and backtesting quantitative models, screening for investment opportunities, and forecasting price movements based on fundamental drivers.

name: Global Seasonal Regime Return Signals
description: This dataset provides predictive return signals for global equities by modeling the impact of calendar seasonality, corporate event timing, market regime context, and key data sources such as price-volume, analyst forecasts, options, and fundamentals. Each module isolates a specific data aspect—like price-volume trends, analyst revisions, or option-implied signals—and overlays contextual features such as month/quarter effects, proximity to earnings or guidance events, and prevailing market regimes (e.g., risk-on/off, expansion/contraction). The dataset is strictly point-in-time and D1-lagged to avoid lookahead bias, making it robust for research and production use. By enabling detailed analysis of how individual features and market contexts drive return predictions, it supports advanced quantitative modeling, event studies, and adaptive strategies across diverse market conditions.

name: Global Corporate Hiring Trends
description: This dataset tracks job opening activity for over 3,300 publicly listed companies worldwide, focusing on those with a market capitalization above $1 billion. It provides daily and historical counts of new and total job openings, along with full-text job descriptions, job types, and geographic details. The data is structured to allow analysis by sector, industry, and company, including subsidiaries and technology trends mentioned in job postings. By monitoring changes in hiring activity, investors can gain early insights into corporate growth, expansion, or contraction, which often precede shifts in revenue, operational momentum, and ultimately, stock price movements. This makes the dataset valuable for forecasting company performance and identifying macroeconomic or sector-specific trends.

name: Smart Insider Transaction Aggregates
description: This dataset provides a structured, matrix-format view of insider trading activity, where individual transactions by company insiders are aggregated and filtered using advanced methodologies. By summarizing key metrics such as average shares bought or sold, and applying smart filters to highlight the most relevant transactions, the dataset enables researchers and investors to efficiently identify patterns of insider behavior across companies and regions. Such aggregated insider activity is a valuable signal for predicting future price movements, as it can reveal informed trading ahead of significant corporate events or shifts in company fundamentals. The matrix structure makes it easier to incorporate these insights into quantitative models and backtesting frameworks, supporting the development of alpha-generating investment strategies.

name: Global Insider Transaction Features
description: This dataset provides comprehensive, structured features derived from global insider transactions, including purchases, sales, awards, and option exercises by company executives, directors, and major shareholders. It covers multiple regions and asset classes, with detailed metadata such as transaction type, insider role, ownership connection, trade significance, and post-transaction holdings. By aggregating and analyzing these transactions, the dataset enables the identification of potentially informative trades, such as opportunistic buying or selling, which can signal future price movements due to information asymmetry. Quantitative models and event studies built on this data can help forecast abnormal returns, enhance alpha generation, and improve risk-adjusted portfolio performance by leveraging the predictive power of insider activity.

name: Aggregated Insider Transaction Matrix
description: This dataset provides a structured matrix of insider transaction data, organized by company, region, and time delay. It aggregates and filters insider buying and selling activities, capturing key metrics such as average buy and sell values, transaction counts, and ratios over configurable time windows. By summarizing insider trades from individuals with privileged access to non-public information, the dataset enables analysts to identify patterns of opportunistic or routine trading, cluster buying, and other signals that may precede significant price movements. The smart aggregation and filtering enhance signal quality, making it a valuable resource for predicting future stock performance, detecting market anomalies, and constructing alpha-generating investment strategies.

name: Global Insider Transaction Aggregates

It captures detailed information on insider trades, including buy and sell activity, transaction types, insider roles, and trade significance, organized by region and time delay. By consolidating and summarizing insider trading patterns, the dataset enables researchers and investors to identify potential signals of future price movements, such as cluster buying or selling by key executives. The aggregation and enhancement of raw insider data into a matrix format make it easier to analyze trends, detect anomalies, and generate predictive signals for alpha generation, supporting both event-driven and quantitative investment strategies.

The data is point-in-time, capturing both original and restated values, and is structured to support robust historical analysis and backtesting. By offering granular, high-quality financials and corporate event data, this dataset enables researchers and investors to build and test predictive models, assess company health, and identify drivers of price movements across global equity markets.

name: Edgar forms data
description: This dataset contains comprehensive SEC filing information sourced from EDGAR, including annual and quarterly reports (10-K, 10-Q), insider transactions (Form 4), institutional holdings (13F), IPO registrations (S-1), and other regulatory filings. It provides detailed metadata such as company identifiers, transaction details, ownership changes, and event classifications. By analyzing these filings, investors and analysts can gain insights into company financial health, insider activity, institutional sentiment, and significant corporate events, all of which are valuable for predicting price movements and identifying potential investment opportunities.

name: Ownership Model Data
description: This dataset provides comprehensive global coverage of equity ownership by institutions, mutual funds, and insiders/stakeholders, with detailed position-level data for each security and holder. It includes both summary and granular holdings, sourced from regulatory filings such as SEC 13F, UK Share Register, and other international disclosures. The data tracks current and historical positions, market values, portfolio characteristics, and investment styles, enabling analysis of ownership trends, concentration, and changes over time. By revealing shifts in institutional and insider holdings, the dataset helps identify informed trading, herding, and market sentiment, which are critical for predicting price movements, liquidity changes, and potential catalysts in global equities.

name: Short Sale Volume Data
description: This dataset provides detailed information on short sale trading activity for U.S. equities, including metrics such as short volume, short exempt volume, total trade volume, and trade-level details like symbol, date, time, size, and price. The data is sourced from multiple trade reporting facilities and covers regular trading hours, offering a comprehensive view of short selling across major U.S. exchanges and off-exchange venues. By analyzing trends in short sale volume relative to total volume, market participants can gauge bearish sentiment, identify potential short squeezes, and anticipate price movements driven by short covering or increased short interest. This dataset is valuable for traders, analysts, and quantitative researchers seeking to enhance predictive models and risk management strategies.

name: Institutions and Beneficial Stake Ownership
description: This dataset provides comprehensive information on global equity ownership by institutions, mutual funds, and beneficial stakeholders. It includes current and historical holdings data from over 50,000 portfolios and companies across 70 countries, with more than 10 years of history. Key fields cover shares held, percent of shares outstanding, report dates, aggregated statistics, and investor profiles. The dataset enables analysis of institutional buying and selling activity, ownership concentration, and changes in major holders, which are critical for understanding market sentiment, liquidity, and potential price movements. By tracking shifts in institutional positions and identifying new or reduced stakes, investors and researchers can anticipate trends, detect accumulation or distribution phases, and enhance predictive models for stock price behavior.

name: Index Reconstitution Data
description: This dataset provides comprehensive information on global index reconstitution events, including the addition and deletion of stocks or companies from various equity indexes, their respective weight percentages, and detailed hedge ratio data. It covers dynamic and static hedge ratios for both indexes and currencies, as well as currency pair exposures and effective dates. The dataset also includes metrics such as momentum and interest rates, along with position weights and returns for index components. By tracking changes in index composition, weights, and hedging strategies, this dataset enables analysts to identify shifts in market sentiment, sector rotation, and currency risk management, which are critical for forecasting price movements and understanding the impact of index rebalancing on asset prices.

The dataset is designed to cover opinion mining tasks including sentiment analysis, company grouping, and value prediction, ultimately seeking to uncover valuable insights from the complete event timeline across diverse text data.
